question: Can I take a job or travel to a place where no Jumu'ah prayer is held?
asked: He has a job offer, but according to his Google research the place has no musalla or masjid. Is he allowed to take the job and travel to a location where it looks like there might not be any Jumu'ah? And more broadly, if he travels anywhere, for any reason, and there's no Jumu'ah there, is that permissible?
answer:
Jumu'ah is of course obligatory on every adult, sane Muslim male who doesn't have an excuse preventing him from attending the Jumu'ah. And Jumu'ah is obligatory if there is a Jumu'ah that is being held in the place that you are at. If there is no Jumu'ah, and there are not enough Muslims to perform a Jumu'ah, then you are not obligated to have a Jumu'ah by yourself. There is no Jumu'ah by yourself; there must be the bare minimum. Now, what is the bare minimum? It depends on madhhab to madhhab. Some say three, some small minority even said two, some said you have to have 40. So you have a different interpretation. That's not the question here.

Suppose that there is no Jumu'ah: there's not enough Muslims, and there are no musallas or masjids where Jumu'ah is being undertaken. Should you go to such a location? The response is very straightforward. Alhamdulillah, Allah has not obligated on us that which we cannot bear. And the obligation of Jumu'ah is binding only when there is a Jumu'ah that is in your locality. The Shari'ah has not obligated you to not find sustenance unless there is a Jumu'ah being held over there. Allah's religion is easy. "There is no difficulty." "Allah wants to make things easy for you." So do not put restrictions that the Shari'ah has not put.

And there are no restrictions to moving to a locality where your sustenance is, where you have a good job offer. I'm assuming, because you're writing from a Muslim-majority country, that the job offer is in some faraway location in another land, for example, and you are not able to find online any musalla there. And so the assumption is that in this non-Muslim land there is no Jumu'ah being performed, so you are now wondering, because of the Jumu'ah issue, should you travel or not?

And the response, as I said, is that there is no haraj, **there is no sin on you to travel for your job, or even to travel for any permissible reason.** Even if it is not a dire situation, you may travel for any permissible reason. And if during the travel Jumu'ah falls and you are still traveling, or you're at a destination or a location where there is no Jumu'ah, then you are not obligated.

And in fact, many scholars... and this is another controversy: what if you're a musafir and there is a Jumu'ah, and you are in the state of safar? Are you obliged to attend or not? Even then there is a controversy, and some fuqaha say the musafir is not obliged to Jumu'ah, even though the position that I feel is more reasonable is that if the musafir has temporarily reached a spot where he is residing, even if it's a day or two, and there is Jumu'ah being held in that city, then he should attend Jumu'ah. But anyway, my point is that the Jumu'ah is not obligatory when there is no Jumu'ah being established, and therefore do not make the absence of a Jumu'ah a cause for you to not take up this job offer.

And also realize that from the beginning of time people have been traveling. The Muslim world has had travelers, and they traveled for reasons that sometimes were religious-based and sometimes were worldly-based. And it is not recorded that they said, "I have to plan a route such that every city I stop in, there must be a musalla over there." No. We have had travelers that have even traveled to the lands of Europe. There was a famous traveler by the name of Ibn Fadlan, and he traveled all the way into the lands of Europe, and he went, they say, even to Norway and other places where he met the Vikings. And then he came back and he wrote about that. Of course, Ibn Battuta as well, the famous traveler: he went all the way across the world, and he came back to his lands in Morocco.

And so all of these, from the time of the Sahabah... In fact, it is even narrated that some of the Sahabah wanted to live away from society and civilization, such as Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, radiAllahu ta'ala anhu. For whatever reason, he just felt that he was more at peace living alone. And so he literally built a hut, a small place, literally in the middle of nowhere. Him and his family, him and his wife actually, settled over there, because he felt that he would rather be living away from society. And it is not reported that he established Jumu'ah or that he traveled far to get to Jumu'ah. He would live where he was, and he was content over there, and he passed away in circumstances that, again, I've discussed in my lectures about the Sahabah.

The point being that there is no obligation on you to choose your job based upon whether there's Jumu'ah or not. If there is Jumu'ah, alhamdulillah. If not, then no problem. You may go to that location, and you will pray dhuhr instead of Jumu'ah.

Now, this is in terms of obligation. I have to also point out here that if you are traveling to a land or a country where it's a very different circumstance, where you're coming from a Muslim majority and now you're going to become a minority, that comes with other factors. And you have to decide whether you feel confident enough, strong enough in your faith, to be able to venture out. There is no question, psychologically speaking (not religiously, psychologically speaking, and they're not necessarily divorced from one another, but I'm just saying psychologically), it is good to be with society, with Muslim communities. There is a barrier of protection that comes when you're in a Muslim land, especially an observant Muslim land, that might not happen when you travel to other places.

And if you're not accustomed to the cultures and the accessibility of certain issues in other lands, you have to think long and hard and then make a choice based upon that. But that's a separate issue from what you asked me about in terms of Jumu'ah; you weigh the pros and cons. And there is no question that if you have a very good job lined up, and you feel confident that inshallah you can be a practicing Muslim, you're going to observe the prayers, there is no question that the Shari'ah does not obligate upon you to find a locality where there is Jumu'ah.

That having been said, I also want to add here a personal anecdote. In fact, my very first job, when I was still doing my chemical engineering degree, when I was based in Houston, Texas, was actually in a small town called Freeport. It is still there; there's a Dow Chemical plant over there. And when I accepted that job (this was back in the mid 90s, early 90s), I found out that there was no Jumu'ah being established in Freeport, Texas. And as I was a student at the time, I asked my teacher the exact same question you are asking me. I said, "I got a very good job offer from Dow Chemical. Can I go and work there? But I'm worried that there is no Jumu'ah." And of course, at that time I was not studying Islam, so I had to ask somebody who was studying Islam, who was obviously my first teacher. And he told me the exact same thing I'm telling you, which is that the Shari'ah is not obligating you to find such a location. So I actually took up that job.

And subhanAllah, this is my point in telling you the story: when I went there, I realized that the reason why there was no Jumu'ah was because nobody had really gathered the Muslims there and started one. And so I literally found out the five, seven Muslims that were working in the plant, and I contacted them, and I said, "Hey, let's do a Jumu'ah together." And alhamdulillah, as a young teenager (I was still 19 at the time), I helped establish Jumu'ah in that small community. And I heard that they continued after me, and I think there's even a musalla or a masjid close by where they can now go and pray.

So my point is: make it your niyyah, "Okay, there is no Jumu'ah there; inshallah, I'm going to go there." And inshallah, for sure, you will find five or ten Muslims scattered around everywhere. You just find them, figure out how you can come together, the best time and place on Friday afternoon, and then inshallah you be the one who starts Jumu'ah, and then starts Islamic activities. And Allah knows where that will lead, years or decades from now. So I hope that, inshallah, answers your question.
